question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-1,1]\times [-1,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=6{x}^{2}y+x+2y-2{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2}. $$ Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[-1,\,1]^{T}.$
$[$ $2$ {{field-1}} $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ $1$ $]$
{{field-2}} $-4$ {{field-3}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(6{x}^{2}y+x+2y-2{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(6{x}^{2}y+x+2y-2{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12xy+1-10x \\ 6{x}^{2}+2-4y\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(12xy+1-10x) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(6{x}^{2}+2-4y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(12xy+1-10x) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(6{x}^{2}+2-4y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12y-10 & 12x \\ 12x & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}12y-10 & 12x \\ 12x & -4\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}12xy+1-10x \\ 6{x}^{2}+2-4y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}12y-10 & 12x \\ 12x & -4\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}12xy+1-10x \\ 6{x}^{2}+2-4y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}12(1)-10 & 12(-1) \\ 12(-1) & -4\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}12(-1)(1)+1-10(-1) \\ 6(-1)^{2}+2-4(1)\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -12 \\ -12 & -4\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
